Tyrosine.definition: A conditionally essential amino acid and precursor to catecholamines (dopamine → norepinephrine → epinephrine) via TH and AADC. Used in ME/CFS for cognitive function and fatigue when catecholamine depletion is suspected; caution in hyperadrenergic states.

doseZones.mechanism: Catecholamine precursor. Supplies tyrosine if rate-limiting for DA/NE production.

Theanine.label: Theanine
Theanine.definition: L-Theanine: a non-proteinogenic amino acid from green tea that crosses the BBB and increases GABA, serotonin, and dopamine levels while promoting alpha brainwave activity (relaxed alertness). Used in ME/CFS for anxiety reduction without sedation and for improving sleep quality.

doseZones.mechanism: Glutamate antagonist + GABA modulator. Promotes calm without sedation.

Ashwagandha.label: Ashwagandha
Ashwagandha.definition: Withania somnifera: an adaptogenic herb used in Ayurveda with cortisol-modulating, GABAergic, and antioxidant effects. Reduces stress-induced cortisol elevation but may lower already-low cortisol in ME/CFS; used for sleep and anxiety.
Ashwagandha.generic: Ashwagandha root extract (Withania somnifera, standardized to withanolides)

doseZones.mechanism: Adaptogen with GABA-A modulation + cortisol reduction. Modulates stress response axis.

Rhodiola.label: Rhodiola
Rhodiola.definition: Rhodiola rosea: an adaptogenic herb used for fatigue, cognitive performance, and stress resilience. Rhodiola may enhance mitochondrial function and modulate serotonin/dopamine. Used in ME/CFS for fatigue and brain fog; activating effect may be poorly tolerated in severe ME/CFS.
Rhodiola.generic: Rhodiola rosea root extract (standardized to rosavins and salidroside)

doseZones.mechanism: Adaptogen with monoamine modulation reducing fatigue perception. Variable evidence.

Cordyceps.label: Cordyceps
Cordyceps.definition: A medicinal mushroom (Cordyceps militaris or C. sinensis) used in traditional Chinese medicine for fatigue and respiratory conditions. Cordyceps contains cordycepin and polysaccharides with immunomodulatory, antioxidant, and mitochondrial-supportive effects. Used in ME/CFS for energy and immune modulation.
Cordyceps.generic: Cordyceps militaris or C. sinensis extract (standardized to cordycepin/polysaccharides)

doseZones.mechanism: Fungal supplement with adenosine-like compounds. Variable evidence; safety concerns with contaminated products.

Lion's Mane.label: Lion's Mane
Lion's Mane.definition: Hericium erinaceus: a medicinal mushroom that stimulates nerve growth factor (NGF) synthesis and promotes neurogenesis. Used in ME/CFS for cognitive dysfunction and peripheral neuropathy; proposed to improve brain fog via NGF-mediated neuronal repair.

doseZones.mechanism: NGF/BDNF induction supporting neuronal health. Research-stage; limited ME/CFS evidence.

Reishi.label: Reishi
Reishi.definition: Ganoderma lucidum: a medicinal mushroom with immunomodulatory polysaccharides (β-glucans) and triterpenes. Reishi has anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and mast cell-stabilizing effects. Used in ME/CFS for immune balance and MCAS symptoms.
Reishi.class: Medicinal mushroom / immunomodulator / mast cell stabilizer

doseZones.mechanism: Immunomodulatory polysaccharides. Variable evidence.

CBD.label: CBD
CBD.definition: Cannabidiol: a non-psychoactive cannabinoid from cannabis/hemp with anti-inflammatory, analgesic, anxiolytic, and anticonvulsant effects. CBD acts on serotonin (5-HT1A agonist), TRPV1, PPARγ, and adenosine receptors. Used in ME/CFS for pain, sleep, anxiety, and neuroinflammation.
CBD.brand: Epidiolex (FDA-approved for epilepsy); various supplement brands

doseZones.mechanism: Multi-target cannabinoid system modulator reducing inflammation/anxiety. Variable response.

THC.label: THC
THC.definition: Delta-9-Tetrahydrocannabinol: the primary psychoactive cannabinoid in cannabis, acting on CB1 and CB2 receptors. Used medically for pain, nausea, appetite stimulation, and sleep. Caution in ME/CFS: may worsen orthostatic intolerance (vasodilation), brain fog, and tachyphylaxis.
THC.brand: Marinol, Syndros (synthetic THC); various medical cannabis products

doseZones.mechanism: CB1/CB2 agonist. Psychoactive. Variable response; dependence risk.
Multi-target cannabinoid system modulator reducing inflammation/anxiety.

Ketamine.label: Ketamine
Ketamine.definition: An NMDA receptor antagonist dissociative anesthetic with rapid-acting antidepressant effects. Low-dose ketamine infusions are used experimentally in ME/CFS and fibromyalgia for central sensitization, neuropathic pain, and treatment-resistant depression. The mechanism involves mTOR-mediated synaptogenesis via AMPA activation.
Ketamine.brand: Ketalar, Spravato (esketamine, nasal spray, FDA-approved for depression)
Ketamine.class: NMDA receptor antagonist / dissociative anesthetic / rapid-acting antidepressant
Ketamine.rx: Prescription only; administered in clinic (IV infusion) or supervised (nasal Spravato)

doseZones.mechanism: NMDA antagonist with rapid neuroplastic effects at sub-anesthetic dose. Research-stage for depression; not established in ME/CFS.
Dissociation/anesthesia without disease-relevant mechanism. Different drug profile, different clinical purpose.

Psilocybin.label: Psilocybin
Psilocybin.definition: A serotonergic psychedelic (prodrug of psilocin, a 5-HT2A agonist) under investigation for depression, anxiety, and cluster headaches. Hypothesized to promote neuroplasticity and disrupt maladaptive neural networks. Not yet studied in ME/CFS; potential relevance to central sensitization and treatment-resistant depression.
Psilocybin.rx: Investigational; Schedule I in US; clinical trial use only. Decriminalized/medical use in limited jurisdictions.
Psilocybin.brand: Investigational — no commercial brand for depression

doseZones.mechanism: 5-HT2A agonist inducing neuroplastic states. Research-stage; not established for ME/CFS.

HIF-1α.label: HIF-1α
HIF-1α.definition: Hypoxia-Inducible Factor 1 Alpha: a transcription factor that coordinates cellular adaptation to low oxygen, upregulating glycolysis, angiogenesis (VEGF), and erythropoiesis. Stabilized by mitochondrial ROS and succinate accumulation; HIF-1α activation may drive the glycolytic shift in ME/CFS.

SC.label: SC
SC.definition: Supercomplex (respirasome): a stable assembly of mitochondrial electron transport chain complexes (I+III₂+IV) that enhances electron transfer efficiency and reduces ROS production. WASF3 overexpression disrupts supercomplex assembly; SC instability may be a direct mechanism for impaired OXPHOS in ME/CFS.

WASF3.label: WASF3
WASF3.definition: Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome Protein Family Member 3: a protein that, when overexpressed, disrupts mitochondrial respiratory supercomplex assembly, impairing OXPHOS efficiency. WASF3 is a candidate driver of mitochondrial dysfunction in ME/CFS — elevated WASF3 → supercomplex destabilization → reduced ATP synthesis → exercise intolerance and PEM.
WASF3.also: Also known as WAVE3; implicated in ME/CFS mitochondrial pathology

3β-HSD.label: 3β-HSD
3β-HSD.definition: 3β-Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase: an enzyme converting pregnenolone to progesterone and DHEA to androstenedione in steroidogenesis. Impaired 3β-HSD activity may alter neurosteroid balance in ME/CFS.
3β-HSD.also: 17β-HSD: converts androstenedione to testosterone and estrone to estradiol

AADC.label: AADC
AADC.definition: Aromatic L-Amino Acid Decarboxylase: the enzyme that converts L-DOPA to dopamine and 5-HTP to serotonin. AADC requires pyridoxal phosphate (vitamin B6) as a cofactor; AADC dysfunction would impair both dopaminergic and serotonergic neurotransmission.

AChE.label: AChE
AChE.definition: Acetylcholinesterase: the enzyme that rapidly hydrolyzes acetylcholine in the synaptic cleft, terminating cholinergic signaling. Inhibited by pyridostigmine (Mestinon) to enhance parasympathetic vagal tone in ME/CFS/POTS.

AIMM.label: AIMM
AIMM.definition: Acquired Ischemic Mitochondrial Myopathy: mitochondrial damage in muscle tissue caused by impaired microvascular oxygen delivery rather than a primary mitochondrial defect. AIMM links endothelial dysfunction → tissue hypoxia → mitochondrial dysfunction in ME/CFS, suggesting the primary lesion may be vascular, not mitochondrial.

ANC.label: ANC
ANC.definition: Absolute Neutrophil Count: the number of neutrophils per microliter of blood. Neutropenia (low ANC) can occur with certain ME/CFS treatments (valacyclovir, rituximab) or as a drug side effect requiring monitoring.

ANT.label: ANT
ANT.definition: Adenine Nucleotide Translocator: the mitochondrial inner membrane transporter exchanging matrix ATP for cytosolic ADP. ANT is a core component of the mPTP and its function is impaired by oxidative stress; ANT dysfunction locks ATP inside failing mitochondria in ME/CFS.

AQP2.label: AQP2
AQP2.definition: Aquaporin-2: the vasopressin-regulated water channel in renal collecting ducts controlling water reabsorption. AQP2 dysfunction or impaired vasopressin signaling may contribute to the nocturia and fluid dysregulation frequently reported in ME/CFS/POTS.

CAP.label: CAP
CAP.definition: Cholinergic Anti-inflammatory Pathway: a vagus nerve-mediated reflex where efferent vagal signals release acetylcholine, which binds α7 nicotinic receptors on splenic macrophages, suppressing TNF-α and other pro-inflammatory cytokines. Impaired CAP (low vagal tone) may permit unchecked peripheral inflammation in ME/CFS.

cGMP.label: cGMP
cGMP.definition: Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate: a second messenger produced by guanylyl cyclase (soluble sGC activated by NO, or particulate pGC activated by natriuretic peptides). cGMP mediates vasodilation via PKG; NO-sGC-cGMP signaling dysfunction may contribute to impaired endothelial vasodilation in ME/CFS.

COMPASS-31.label: COMPASS-31
COMPASS-31.definition: Composite Autonomic Symptom Score 31. A validated 31-item patient questionnaire assessing autonomic symptom severity across 6 domains — orthostatic intolerance, vasomotor, secretomotor (sweating), gastrointestinal, bladder, and pupillomotor function — with a 1-month recall period.

COX-2.label: COX-2
COX-2.definition: Cyclooxygenase-2: the inducible isoform of COX, upregulated by inflammatory stimuli (cytokines, NF-κB), producing prostaglandins (PGE2, PGI2) that mediate pain, fever, and inflammation. COX-2 is induced in ME/CFS neuroinflammation and is a therapeutic target of NSAIDs and celecoxib.

CYP.label: CYP
CYP.definition: Cytochrome P450: a superfamily of heme-containing enzymes responsible for Phase I metabolism of most drugs, steroid hormones, and xenobiotics. CYP polymorphisms (CYP2D6, CYP2C19, CYP3A4) explain variability in drug response and side-effect susceptibility in ME/CFS patients.
CYP.also: CYP3A4 (metabolizes ~50% of drugs), CYP2D6 (antidepressants, beta-blockers), CYP2C19 (proton pump inhibitors)

CysLT1.label: CysLT1
CysLT1.definition: Cysteinyl Leukotriene Receptor Type 1: the receptor mediating the bronchoconstrictor and pro-inflammatory effects of cysteinyl leukotrienes (LTC4, LTD4, LTE4) released by mast cells. CysLT1 is the target of montelukast (Singulair), used in ME/CFS/MCAS to block mast-cell-driven respiratory and systemic symptoms.

DAMI.label: DAMI
DAMI.definition: Dopaminergic Asymmetry Measurement Index: a composite biomarker integrating striatal FDG-PET asymmetry, COMPASS-31 autonomic symptom score, and aripiprazole response slope. DAMI aims to quantify the degree of lateralized dopaminergic dysfunction in ME/CFS — high asymmetry correlates with specific autonomic and motor symptom patterns.

DBH.label: DBH
DBH.definition: Dopamine-Beta-Hydroxylase: the enzyme that converts dopamine to norepinephrine inside synaptic vesicles. DBH is released with norepinephrine during sympathetic activation; serum DBH activity reflects sympathetic tone and may be elevated in hyperadrenergic ME/CFS/POTS subtypes.

DCA.label: DCA
DCA.definition: Dichloroacetate: a PDK inhibitor that reactivates pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH), shifting metabolism from glycolysis back toward glucose oxidation. DCA has been proposed experimentally for ME/CFS to reverse the PDK-mediated glycolytic lock. Narrow therapeutic window — causes reversible peripheral neuropathy.
DCA.rx: Investigational; not commercially available as a pharmaceutical

doseZones.mechanism: PDK inhibitor restoring PDH activity and pyruvate entry into TCA cycle. Neurotoxicity risk at cumulative dose.

DDR.label: DDR
DDR.definition: Discoidin Domain Receptor: a family of collagen-activated receptor tyrosine kinases (DDR1, DDR2) regulating cell adhesion, migration, and ECM remodeling. DDR signaling is implicated in tissue fibrosis and may be relevant to connective tissue pathology in ME/CFS/EDS.

DMF.label: DMF
DMF.definition: Dimethyl Fumarate: an immunomodulator activating NRF2 (the antioxidant master regulator) and shifting immune responses from Th1/Th17 toward Th2. FDA-approved for multiple sclerosis; of interest in ME/CFS for its dual NRF2-activating and immunomodulatory effects.

doseZones.mechanism: Nrf2 activator + immunomodulator. Activates endogenous anti-inflammatory programs via Keap1 modification.

DMV.label: DMV
DMV.definition: Dorsal Motor Nucleus of Vagus: a brainstem nucleus containing parasympathetic preganglionic neurons that project via the vagus nerve to the heart, lungs, and GI tract. DMV dysfunction may impair vagal parasympathetic output in ME/CFS, contributing to tachycardia, gastroparesis, and reduced anti-inflammatory cholinergic tone.

DPP-4.label: DPP-4
DPP-4.definition: Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (CD26): a serine protease that rapidly degrades incretin hormones (GLP-1, GIP), limiting their insulinotropic effects. DPP-4 also exists as soluble CD26, a T-cell activation marker elevated in some autoimmune conditions, and cleaves multiple chemokines. DPP-4 inhibitors (sitagliptin) are used in diabetes; DPP-4/CD26 dysregulation may link metabolic and immune dysfunction in ME/CFS.

DRG.label: DRG
DRG.definition: Dorsal Root Ganglion: a cluster of sensory neuron cell bodies along the spinal cord that transmit pain, temperature, and touch signals. DRG neurons express TRPV1, TRPA1, and PIEZO2; DRG sensitization is a key site of peripheral pain amplification in ME/CFS and fibromyalgia.

DTBZ.label: DTBZ
DTBZ.definition: Dihydrotetrabenazine: a PET radioligand that binds to VMAT2 on presynaptic monoamine terminals, used to quantify dopaminergic neuron density. Reduced striatal DTBZ binding in ME/CFS would indicate dopaminergic terminal loss — a finding linking ME/CFS fatigue to Parkinsonian pathophysiology.

EC cells.label: EC cells
EC cells.definition: Enterochromaffin Cells: specialized gut epithelial cells that produce ~95% of the body's serotonin via TPH1. EC cell serotonin regulates gut motility, secretion, and vagal afferent signaling. EC cell dysfunction may link gut dysbiosis to altered serotonergic signaling in ME/CFS.

ECM.label: ECM
ECM.definition: Extracellular Matrix: the network of collagen, elastin, proteoglycans, and glycoproteins that provides structural support to tissues. ECM abnormalities (collagen defects, MMP dysregulation) are central to hypermobility spectrum disorders (EDS/HSD) commonly comorbid with ME/CFS.

ET-1.label: ET-1
ET-1.definition: Endothelin-1: a potent vasoconstrictor peptide produced by endothelial cells, acting on ETA (vasoconstriction) and ETB (vasodilation via NO) receptors. ET-1 is elevated in ME/CFS and may drive microvascular constriction, contributing to tissue hypoperfusion and exercise intolerance.

ETA.label: ETA
ETA.definition: Endothelin Receptor Type A: mediates the vasoconstrictor effects of endothelin-1 on vascular smooth muscle. ETA overactivation may contribute to microvascular dysfunction and tissue ischemia in ME/CFS. ETA receptor autoantibodies have been identified in subsets of ME/CFS patients.

FAO.label: FAO
FAO.definition: Fatty Acid Oxidation (β-oxidation): the mitochondrial breakdown of fatty acids to acetyl-CoA for the TCA cycle. Impaired FAO in ME/CFS forces reliance on glycolysis, reducing ATP yield per substrate molecule and accelerating fatigue during prolonged activity.

FDG.label: FDG
FDG.definition: Fluorodeoxyglucose (¹⁸F-FDG): a radioactive glucose analogue used in PET imaging to measure tissue metabolic activity. FDG-PET in ME/CFS reveals regional hypometabolism in the brainstem, frontal cortex, and striatum, correlating with cognitive and fatigue severity.

G-CSF.label: G-CSF
G-CSF.definition: Granulocyte Colony-Stimulating Factor: a cytokine stimulating neutrophil production and mobilization from bone marrow. G-CSF is elevated in some ME/CFS cohorts and may contribute to the low-grade inflammatory state.

GI.label: GI
GI.definition: Gastrointestinal: pertaining to the digestive tract. GI symptoms (bloating, pain, nausea, altered motility, SIBO, GERD) are among the most common and disabling non-core symptoms in ME/CFS.

GLP-1.label: GLP-1
GLP-1.definition: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1: an incretin hormone released from intestinal L-cells after meals, enhancing insulin secretion, slowing gastric emptying, and promoting satiety. GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide) are diabetes/obesity drugs; GLP-1 has neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory properties that may be relevant to ME/CFS metabolic dysfunction.

Gαq.label: Gαq
Gαq.definition: G Protein Alpha-q Subunit: the α subunit of the Gq heterotrimeric G protein, which activates phospholipase C-β (PLC-β) upon GPCR stimulation, producing IP3 (calcium release) and DAG (PKC activation). Gαq-coupled receptors include H1 (histamine), M1/M3 (muscarinic), AT1 (angiotensin), and α1-adrenergic receptors — all implicated in ME/CFS autonomic and immune dysfunction.

HCA2.label: HCA2
HCA2.definition: Hydroxycarboxylic Acid Receptor 2 (GPR109A): a Gαi-coupled receptor activated by niacin (vitamin B3) and β-hydroxybutyrate (ketone body). Expressed on mast cells, adipocytes, and immune cells; HCA2 activation on mast cells mediates the niacin flush (PGD2 release). Also mediates the anti-inflammatory effects of ketone bodies — relevant to ketogenic diet strategies in ME/CFS.

HCN.label: HCN
HCN.definition: Hyperpolarization-activated Cyclic Nucleotide-gated channel: the channel carrying the If ('funny') current in cardiac pacemaker cells (SA node) and neurons. cAMP directly activates HCN channels, accelerating heart rate. HCN blockade by ivabradine is used therapeutically in ME/CFS/POTS to reduce sinus tachycardia without lowering blood pressure.

hEDS.label: hEDS
hEDS.definition: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome: the most common subtype of EDS, characterized by generalized joint hypermobility, musculoskeletal pain, skin fragility, and dysautonomia. hEDS is strongly comorbid with ME/CFS and POTS; distinguishing features include the Beighton score, atrophic scarring, and positive family history.
hEDS.also: See EDS (Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome); HSD (Hypermobility Spectrum Disorder)

HIT.label: HIT
HIT.definition: Histamine Intolerance: a condition where histamine ingestion or release exceeds degradation capacity (impaired DAO/HNMT enzymes), causing flushing, headache, tachycardia, GI symptoms, and nasal congestion. Frequently comorbid with ME/CFS and MCAS; managed with low-histamine diet and DAO supplementation.
HIT.also: Not to be confused with Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia

HSC.label: HSC
HSC.definition: Haematopoietic Stem Cell: multipotent stem cells in bone marrow that give rise to all blood cell lineages. HSC dysfunction or exhaustion has been hypothesized in ME/CFS as a mechanism for persistent immune abnormalities, though direct evidence is lacking.

HSP70.label: HSP70
HSP70.definition: Heat Shock Protein 70: a molecular chaperone that refolds misfolded proteins and prevents aggregation under cellular stress. HSP70 is released extracellularly as a DAMP, activating TLR2/TLR4. Elevated extracellular HSP70 in ME/CFS may reflect chronic cellular stress and contribute to sterile inflammation.

HTN.label: HTN
HTN.definition: Hypertension: chronically elevated blood pressure. Paradoxically present in some hyperadrenergic ME/CFS/POTS patients despite orthostatic intolerance; supine hypertension with orthostatic hypotension/tachycardia complicates pharmacological management.

H₂S.label: H₂S
H₂S.definition: Hydrogen Sulfide: a gaseous signaling molecule (gasotransmitter) with dual roles — at physiological levels, H₂S is a vasodilator, mitochondrial electron donor (at Complex II), and antioxidant; at excess levels from gut dysbiosis (sulfate-reducing bacteria), H₂S is a mitochondrial toxin inhibiting Complex IV. H₂S dysregulation links gut dysbiosis to mitochondrial dysfunction in ME/CFS.

IA.label: IA
IA.definition: Immunoadsorption: a therapeutic apheresis procedure that selectively removes pathogenic antibodies (IgG) from plasma while returning other plasma components. Used experimentally in ME/CFS to test whether removal of GPCR autoantibodies improves autonomic and fatigue symptoms; temporary benefit suggests autoantibody-mediated pathophysiology in responsive patients.

IENFD.label: IENFD
IENFD.definition: Intraepidermal Nerve Fiber Density: the number of small unmyelinated nerve fibers per millimeter of epidermis, measured by skin punch biopsy with PGP9.5 immunostaining. Reduced IENFD is the gold-standard diagnostic marker for small-fiber neuropathy, found in a significant subset of ME/CFS patients, linking to neuropathic pain and autonomic dysfunction.

IgE.label: IgE
IgE.definition: Immunoglobulin E: the antibody isotype mediating allergic responses by binding to high-affinity FcεRI receptors on mast cells and basophils. Elevated IgE in ME/CFS may indicate an atopic/MCAS endotype; however, most MCAS presents with normal IgE.

IgG.label: IgG
IgG.definition: Immunoglobulin G — the most abundant antibody class in blood, providing long-term immunity and able to cross the placenta.

IL.label: IL
IL.definition: Interleukin: a broad family of cytokines primarily mediating communication between leukocytes. Key interleukins in ME/CFS include IL-1β (pro-inflammatory, sickness behavior), IL-6 (fatigue, neuroinflammation), IL-10 (anti-inflammatory, often reduced), and IL-17 (Th17, gut barrier).

ILMI.label: ILMI
ILMI.definition: Ipsilateral Limb Metabolic Index: a measure comparing FDG-PET glucose uptake between left and right limb muscles, quantifying metabolic asymmetry. Abnormal ILMI suggests lateralized mitochondrial or vascular dysfunction — a novel biomarker approach in ME/CFS.

IMPase.label: IMPase
IMPase.definition: Inositol Monophosphatase: the enzyme that regenerates free inositol from inositol monophosphate, a critical step in the phosphatidylinositol (PI) cycle. IMPase is inhibited by lithium; this inhibition depletes PIP2, reducing IP3/DAG second messenger production and attenuating Gαq-coupled receptor signaling — a mechanism by which lithium may modulate hyperactive GPCR signaling in ME/CFS.

IP receptor.label: IP receptor
IP receptor.definition: Prostacyclin I2 Receptor: a Gαs-coupled receptor activated by prostacyclin (PGI2), mediating vasodilation and inhibition of platelet aggregation. IP receptor dysfunction or impaired PGI2 synthesis by endothelial COX-2 may contribute to microvascular constriction in ME/CFS.

KAT.label: KAT
KAT.definition: Kynurenine Aminotransferase: the enzyme that converts kynurenine to kynurenic acid (KYNA), the neuroprotective NMDA receptor antagonist branch of the kynurenine pathway. KAT activity determines the KYNA/QUIN balance; impaired KAT shifts toward QUIN-mediated excitotoxicity in ME/CFS neuroinflammation.

KMO.label: KMO
KMO.definition: Kynurenine 3-Monooxygenase: the enzyme that diverts kynurenine toward the neurotoxic QUIN branch (via 3-hydroxykynurenine). KMO is the key branch-point enzyme in the kynurenine pathway; KMO upregulation by IFN-γ shifts metabolism toward QUIN (excitotoxic NMDA agonist) and away from KYNA (neuroprotective NMDA antagonist), contributing to excitotoxicity and cognitive dysfunction in ME/CFS.

LC-NE.label: LC-NE
LC-NE.definition: Locus Coeruleus-Norepinephrine system: the brainstem nucleus (LC) that is the primary source of norepinephrine in the CNS, projecting widely to cortex, thalamus, and spinal cord. The LC-NE system regulates arousal, attention, stress responses, and sympathetic tone; LC hyperactivity at night drives the 'tired but wired' state in ME/CFS.

LTD4.label: LTD4
LTD4.definition: Leukotriene D4: a potent cysteinyl leukotriene released by mast cells that causes sustained bronchoconstriction (1000× more potent than histamine), increased vascular permeability, and mucous secretion. LTD4 is a major mediator of MCAS respiratory symptoms; CysLT1 blockade by montelukast targets LTD4 signaling.

LTP.label: LTP
LTP.definition: Long-Term Potentiation: a persistent strengthening of synaptic connections based on recent patterns of activity, considered the cellular basis of learning and memory. Impaired LTP in ME/CFS (via NMDA receptor dysfunction, neuroinflammation, or reduced BDNF) may underlie the cognitive dysfunction and 'brain fog' that patients report as difficulty learning new information.

MAO-B.label: MAO-B
MAO-B.definition: Monoamine Oxidase B: the MAO isoform that preferentially degrades dopamine (and phenylethylamine). MAO-B activity increases with age and in neuroinflammation; elevated MAO-B may contribute to dopamine depletion in ME/CFS. MAO-B inhibitors (selegiline, rasagiline) are used in Parkinson's disease.

MMP.label: MMP
MMP.definition: Matrix Metalloproteinase: a family of zinc-dependent endopeptidases that degrade extracellular matrix proteins (collagen, elastin, proteoglycans). MMP-2 and MMP-9 are elevated in ME/CFS and may contribute to blood-brain barrier disruption, tissue remodeling in hypermobility, and cleavage of cytokines/receptors.

mPTP.label: mPTP
mPTP.definition: Mitochondrial Permeability Transition Pore: a high-conductance channel in the mitochondrial inner membrane that opens under conditions of calcium overload, oxidative stress, and ATP depletion. mPTP opening dissipates the proton gradient, halts ATP synthesis, and releases pro-apoptotic factors. mPTP opening is a candidate terminal mechanism for the acute energy failure in PEM.

MRGPRX2.label: MRGPRX2
MRGPRX2.definition: Mas-related G Protein-Coupled Receptor X2: a mast-cell-specific receptor activated by basic secretagogues (compound 48/80, substance P, certain drugs including quinolones, vancomycin, and neuromuscular blockers). MRGPRX2 mediates IgE-independent mast cell degranulation — a mechanism by which certain medications, stress (substance P), and endogenous peptides could trigger MCAS flares in ME/CFS without requiring allergen sensitization.

MRS.label: MRS
MRS.definition: Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy: an MRI technique measuring brain metabolite concentrations (lactate, NAA, choline, creatine, glutamate, GABA). MRS in ME/CFS has revealed elevated brain lactate, reduced NAA (indicating neuronal dysfunction), and altered glutamate/GABA ratios.

mTORC1.label: mTORC1
mTORC1.definition: Mechanistic Target of Rapamycin Complex 1: an anabolic signaling complex that promotes protein synthesis, lipid synthesis, and mitochondrial biogenesis while inhibiting autophagy. mTORC1 is activated by nutrients, growth factors, and energy status. mTORC1 overactivation in ME/CFS could inhibit autophagy/mitophagy, leading to accumulation of damaged mitochondria.
mTORC1.also: mTORC2: regulates cell survival, cytoskeleton, and Akt activation

NCLX.label: NCLX
NCLX.definition: Mitochondrial Sodium/Calcium/Lithium Exchanger: the primary calcium efflux mechanism from the mitochondrial matrix, exchanging intramitochondrial Ca²⁺ or Li⁺ for cytosolic Na⁺. NCLX inhibition by lithium prolongs mitochondrial calcium retention, potentially enhancing ATP production but also increasing mPTP opening risk. NCLX is the molecular entry point for lithium's effects on mitochondrial calcium handling in ME/CFS research.

NCX1.label: NCX1
NCX1.definition: Sodium/Calcium Exchanger 1: the primary plasma membrane transporter extruding one Ca²⁺ ion in exchange for three Na⁺ ions. NCX1 is critical for calcium homeostasis in cardiomyocytes and neurons; NCX1 dysfunction may contribute to calcium overload and impaired contractility in ME/CFS muscle and vascular smooth muscle.

NHE1.label: NHE1
NHE1.definition: Sodium/Hydrogen Exchanger 1: the ubiquitous plasma membrane transporter exchanging intracellular H⁺ for extracellular Na⁺, regulating intracellular pH and cell volume. NHE1 is activated by oxidative stress and inflammation; sustained NHE1 activation in ME/CFS may contribute to intracellular sodium overload and altered cellular energetics.

NK cell.label: NK cell
NK cell.definition: Natural Killer Cell: a cytotoxic lymphocyte of the innate immune system that kills virus-infected and tumor cells without prior sensitization. Reduced NK cell cytotoxic function (but not number) is one of the most consistently replicated immune abnormalities in ME/CFS, suggesting impaired innate antiviral surveillance.

Nrf2.label: Nrf2
Nrf2.definition: Nuclear Factor Erythroid 2-Related Factor 2: the master transcriptional regulator of the antioxidant response, controlling expression of glutathione synthesis enzymes, thioredoxin, HO-1, NQO1, and phase II detoxification enzymes. Impaired Nrf2 activation in ME/CFS leads to reduced antioxidant capacity, exacerbating oxidative stress — a pathway therapeutically targeted by DMF, sulforaphane, and curcumin.
Nrf2.also: See NRF2 entry for canonical form

NTS.label: NTS
NTS.definition: Nucleus Tractus Solitarius: the primary visceral sensory nucleus in the brainstem, receiving afferent input from the vagus nerve (baroreceptors, chemoreceptors, gut stretch, immune signals). The NTS integrates visceral information and projects to the DMV (parasympathetic output) and RVLM (sympathetic output). NTS dysfunction may impair baroreflex sensitivity and autonomic integration in ME/CFS.

OH.label: OH
OH.definition: Orthostatic Hypotension: a sustained drop in systolic BP ≥20 mmHg or diastolic BP ≥10 mmHg within 3 minutes of standing. OH is a form of orthostatic intolerance distinct from POTS; some ME/CFS patients have OH, others have POTS, and some have both or neither.

PDE4.label: PDE4
PDE4.definition: Phosphodiesterase 4: the predominant cAMP-degrading enzyme in immune and inflammatory cells. PDE4 inhibitors (roflumilast, apremilast) increase cAMP, suppressing TNF-α and other pro-inflammatory cytokines. PDE4 is of interest in ME/CFS for its role in regulating cAMP/PKA signaling and inflammatory tone.

PEA.label: PEA
PEA.definition: Palmitoylethanolamide: an endogenous fatty acid amide that activates PPAR-α, producing analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects via mast cell stabilization and reduced microglial activation. PEA is used in ME/CFS and fibromyalgia for neuropathic pain and neuroinflammation.
PEA.class: Endogenous fatty acid amide / PPAR-α agonist

doseZones.mechanism: Endogenous PPAR-α agonist + mast cell stabilizer. Modulates neuroinflammation through endogenous lipid signaling.

PFC.label: PFC
PFC.definition: Prefrontal Cortex: the anterior frontal lobes mediating executive function, working memory, decision-making, and attention. PFC hypoperfusion and altered functional connectivity are consistently reported in ME/CFS neuroimaging, correlating with cognitive symptom severity.

PGD2.label: PGD2
PGD2.definition: Prostaglandin D2: the primary prostaglandin produced by mast cells upon activation, via hematopoietic PGD2 synthase. PGD2 mediates vasodilation, bronchoconstriction, and sleep regulation; elevated urinary PGD2 metabolites are a biomarker of MCAS and may be useful in identifying ME/CFS patients with a mast-cell-driven endotype.

PGDS.label: PGDS
PGDS.definition: Prostaglandin D2 Synthase: the enzyme converting PGH2 to PGD2. The hematopoietic isoform (H-PGDS) is expressed in mast cells; the lipocalin-type (L-PGDS) is in the CNS. Mast-cell PGDS activity determines PGD2 production — elevated in MCAS and potentially in ME/CFS endotypes with mast cell involvement.

PGE2.label: PGE2
PGE2.definition: Prostaglandin E2: the most abundant prostaglandin, produced by COX-2 and PGE2 synthases. PGE2 mediates inflammation, pain (sensitizes TRPV1), fever (hypothalamus), and vasodilation. Elevated PGE2 in ME/CFS may drive pain sensitization and neuroinflammatory symptoms.

PGH2.label: PGH2
PGH2.definition: Prostaglandin H2: the unstable intermediate produced by COX-1/COX-2 from arachidonic acid. PGH2 is the common precursor for all prostaglandins (PGD2, PGE2, PGF2α, PGI2) and thromboxane (TXA2) — the branch point where COX activity diverges into different lipid mediator profiles that determine the inflammatory phenotype.

PLA2.label: PLA2
PLA2.definition: Phospholipase A2: the enzyme that liberates arachidonic acid from membrane phospholipids, the rate-limiting step in prostaglandin and leukotriene synthesis. PLA2 is activated by calcium, oxidative stress, and inflammatory signals; PLA2 overactivation in ME/CFS may drive excessive pro-inflammatory eicosanoid production.

PLC-β.label: PLC-β
PLC-β.definition: Phospholipase C Beta: the enzyme activated by Gαq-coupled GPCRs, cleaving PIP2 into IP3 (triggers ER Ca²⁺ release) and DAG (activates PKC). PLC-β is the signaling hub for histamine (H1), angiotensin (AT1), and norepinephrine (α1) receptors — all hyperactive in subsets of ME/CFS.

PPAR-alpha.label: PPAR-alpha
PPAR-alpha.definition: Peroxisome Proliferator-Activated Receptor Alpha: a nuclear receptor regulating fatty acid oxidation, ketogenesis, and anti-inflammatory responses. PPAR-α is activated by PEA (palmitoylethanolamide) and fibrates. PPAR-α activation reduces NF-κB-driven inflammation — of interest in ME/CFS metabolic and neuroinflammatory dysfunction.
PPAR-alpha.also: See PPAR for the receptor family

REE.label: REE
REE.definition: Resting Energy Expenditure: the calories the body burns at complete rest, measured by indirect calorimetry. Some studies report paradoxically elevated REE in ME/CFS despite profound fatigue and reduced activity, suggesting a hypermetabolic state driven by immune activation or mitochondrial inefficiency.

RVLM.label: RVLM
RVLM.definition: Rostral Ventrolateral Medulla: the primary sympathetic output nucleus in the brainstem, containing presympathetic neurons that drive tonic and reflex sympathetic vasomotor tone. RVLM overactivity may drive sustained sympathetic activation in ME/CFS, contributing to tachycardia and vasoconstriction at rest.

S100B.label: S100B
S100B.definition: S100 Calcium-Binding Protein B: an astrocyte-derived protein released during brain injury or neuroinflammation. Elevated serum S100B in ME/CFS suggests astrocyte damage or blood-brain barrier disruption, and may correlate with cognitive dysfunction severity.

SA node.label: SA node
SA node.definition: Sinoatrial Node: the heart's natural pacemaker in the right atrium, generating spontaneous action potentials via HCN channels (If current). SA node automaticity is modulated by sympathetic (NE → β1 → faster rate) and parasympathetic (ACh → M2 → slower rate) input; SA node dysfunction or excessive sympathetic drive produces inappropriate sinus tachycardia in ME/CFS/POTS.

sigma1R.label: sigma1R
sigma1R.definition: Sigma-1 Receptor: an endoplasmic reticulum chaperone protein activated by cellular stress, regulating calcium signaling, autophagy, ER stress responses, and mitochondrial-ER contact sites. sigma1R activation is neuroprotective; sigma1R dysfunction may impair the integrated stress response in ME/CFS. Fluvoxamine is a potent sigma1R agonist.

SkQ1.label: SkQ1
SkQ1.definition: Plastoquinonyl-decyl-triphenylphosphonium: a mitochondrial-targeted antioxidant that accumulates in the mitochondrial matrix (driven by membrane potential) and neutralizes ROS at their source. SkQ1 has been proposed experimentally for ME/CFS to directly reduce mitochondrial oxidative stress.

doseZones.mechanism: Mitochondria-targeted antioxidant reducing mitochondrial ROS at source. Research-stage.

SV2A.label: SV2A
SV2A.definition: Synaptic Vesicle Glycoprotein 2A: a transmembrane protein on synaptic vesicles regulating neurotransmitter release. SV2A is the binding site of levetiracetam (Keppra), which modulates SV2A to reduce excessive glutamate release. Levetiracetam's off-label use for ME/CFS brain fog targets SV2A-mediated neurotransmitter modulation.

taVNS.label: taVNS
taVNS.definition: Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation: a non-invasive method of vagus nerve stimulation via electrodes placed on the auricular branch of the vagus nerve in the ear. taVNS increases parasympathetic tone, activates the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway, and may reduce sympathetic overactivation; investigational for ME/CFS/POTS autonomic dysfunction.

TPH1.label: TPH1
TPH1.definition: Tryptophan Hydroxylase 1: the peripheral isoform of TPH, expressed in gut enterochromaffin cells, producing ~95% of the body's serotonin. TPH1-derived serotonin regulates gut motility and is taken up by platelets. TPH1 dysfunction may link gut dysbiosis to altered peripheral serotonin in ME/CFS.
TPH1.also: TPH2: neuronal isoform expressed in raphe nuclei, producing CNS serotonin

TXA2.label: TXA2
TXA2.definition: Thromboxane A2: a platelet-derived eicosanoid produced by COX-1 from arachidonic acid (via thromboxane synthase). TXA2 is a potent vasoconstrictor and platelet aggregator. Altered TXA2/prostacyclin (PGI2) balance may contribute to microvascular dysfunction and platelet hyperactivity in ME/CFS.

VLM.label: VLM
VLM.definition: Ventrolateral Medulla: the brainstem region containing both the rostral VLM (RVLM, sympathetic output) and caudal VLM (CVLM, sympathoinhibitory). VLM dysfunction impairs the baroreflex and autonomic regulation of blood pressure, directly contributing to orthostatic intolerance in ME/CFS.

VMAT2.label: VMAT2
VMAT2.definition: Vesicular Monoamine Transporter 2: the transporter that packages dopamine, norepinephrine, serotonin, and histamine into synaptic vesicles for release. DTBZ-PET measures VMAT2 density as a proxy for monoaminergic neuron integrity. VMAT2 dysfunction could impair neurotransmitter storage and release in ME/CFS.

ΔΨm.label: ΔΨm
ΔΨm.definition: Mitochondrial Membrane Potential: the electrical potential difference across the inner mitochondrial membrane (~−180 mV), generated by the electron transport chain pumping protons. ΔΨm is the driving force for ATP synthesis; mitochondrial depolarization (reduced ΔΨm) has been reported in ME/CFS and may be a direct consequence of oxidative damage, mPTP opening, or respiratory chain dysfunction.

Sertraline.label: Sertraline
Sertraline.definition: An SSRI antidepressant with additional dopamine transporter (DAT) inhibition at higher doses. Used in ME/CFS for comorbid depression and anxiety. Generally well-tolerated but may cause GI side effects and sexual dysfunction.

doseZones.mechanism: SSRI increasing synaptic serotonin. Compensates for deficient serotonin tone.

Fluvoxamine.label: Fluvoxamine
Fluvoxamine.definition: An SSRI antidepressant that is also a potent sigma-1 receptor agonist, with anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects. Of particular interest in ME/CFS and Long COVID for sigma-1R-mediated ER stress reduction and autophagy modulation.
Fluvoxamine.class: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) / sigma-1 receptor agonist

doseZones.mechanism: S1R agonism reducing ER stress and ISR activity. Anti-inflammatory via S1R, not serotonin reuptake at low dose.
SSRI dose — serotonin reuptake inhibition dominates. Different mechanism profile at antidepressant dosing.

Escitalopram.label: Escitalopram
Escitalopram.definition: The S-enantiomer of citalopram, a highly selective SSRI with fewer drug interactions than fluoxetine or paroxetine. Used in ME/CFS for comorbid depression and anxiety.

doseZones.mechanism: SSRI increasing synaptic serotonin. Compensates for deficient serotonin tone.

Desvenlafaxine.label: Desvenlafaxine
Desvenlafaxine.definition: The active metabolite of venlafaxine, an SNRI with more consistent pharmacokinetics and fewer CYP2D6 interactions. Used in ME/CFS for pain, fatigue, and depression.

doseZones.mechanism: SNRI increasing synaptic 5-HT and NE. Compensates for deficient monoamine tone.

Prednisolone.label: Prednisolone
Prednisolone.definition: The active metabolite of prednisone, a glucocorticoid immunosuppressant. Used in autoimmune conditions; in ME/CFS, anecdotal use for inflammatory flares. No RCT evidence; short-term benefit may occur in immune-mediated subsets but chronic use is not recommended.

doseZones.mechanism: Physiological replacement — restores deficient cortisol if HPA axis hypofunctional.
Immunosuppressive — broad inflammation suppression; HPA suppression risk.

Oxycodone.label: Oxycodone
Oxycodone.definition: A semi-synthetic opioid analgesic. Rarely used in ME/CFS due to high dependence liability, opioid-induced hyperalgesia, and worsening of constipation/GI dysmotility.

doseZones.mechanism: Mu-opioid agonist. Suppresses pain perception without reducing nociceptive driver. Dependence, tolerance, OIH risk.

Meloxicam.label: Meloxicam
Meloxicam.definition: A preferential COX-2 inhibitor NSAID with lower GI toxicity than ibuprofen. Used in ME/CFS for inflammatory and joint pain; once-daily dosing improves compliance.

doseZones.mechanism: Preferential COX-2 inhibitor. Anti-inflammatory. Cardiovascular/GI risk.

L-Carnitine.label: L-Carnitine
L-Carnitine.definition: A quaternary ammonium compound that transports long-chain fatty acids into the mitochondrial matrix for β-oxidation. Supplementation may improve energy production in mitochondrial dysfunction; investigated for fatigue in ME/CFS.
L-Carnitine.generic: L-Carnitine (also available as acetyl-L-carnitine [ALCAR] with better CNS penetration)

doseZones.mechanism: Carnitine shuttle transports fatty acids across the inner mitochondrial membrane, supporting β-oxidation and ATP production.

Allopregnanolone.label: Allopregnanolone
Allopregnanolone.definition: An endogenous neurosteroid and potent GABA-A receptor positive allosteric modulator, produced from progesterone. Allopregnanolone has anxiolytic, sedative, and neuroprotective effects. FDA-approved as brexanolone for postpartum depression; of interest in ME/CFS for sleep disturbance and GABAergic dysfunction.
Allopregnanolone.rx: Prescription (US); administered in supervised healthcare setting

doseZones.mechanism: GABA-A neurosteroid site PAM. If deficiency confirmed, replacement is substrate-repletion; otherwise threshold-modulatory.

Ambroxol.label: Ambroxol
Ambroxol.definition: A mucolytic agent that also modulates TRPV1 and TRPM8 cation channels and enhances glucocerebrosidase activity. Proposed experimentally in ME/CFS for TRP channelopathy — TRPV1/TRPM8 dysregulation contributes to temperature dysregulation and pain.

doseZones.mechanism: TRPV1 antagonist reducing muscle pain and PEM. Mucolytic if airway symptoms.

Amlodipine.label: Amlodipine
Amlodipine.definition: An L-type calcium channel blocker (dihydropyridine) used as an antihypertensive. Relevant to ME/CFS downstream of arteriolar TRPV1-mediated vasoconstriction — blocking L-type channels may counteract the vascular component of PEM.

doseZones.mechanism: L-type Ca²⁺ channel blocker reducing TRPV1-mediated vasoconstriction downstream. Does not correct TRPV1 dysfunction.

Anakinra.label: Anakinra
Anakinra.definition: A recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra) blocking both IL-1α and IL-1β signaling. Tested in ME/CFS clinical trials for inflammatory subsets; targets the cytokine sickness-behavior pathway believed to drive fatigue, pain, and cognitive dysfunction.

doseZones.mechanism: Blocks IL-1 receptor, interrupting IL-1β-driven autoinflammatory amplification. Does not address IL-1β source.

Apixaban.label: Apixaban
Apixaban.definition: A direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) inhibiting factor Xa. Proposed experimentally in ME/CFS for microclot-mediated tissue hypoperfusion — the amyloid fibrin microclot hypothesis suggests anticoagulation may improve oxygen delivery.

doseZones.mechanism: Factor Xa inhibitor reducing microthrombi formation. Bleeding risk; research-stage.

Atomoxetine.label: Atomoxetine
Atomoxetine.definition: A selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (NRI) used for ADHD. Used off-label in ME/CFS for cognitive dysfunction and fatigue; increases prefrontal norepinephrine and dopamine without the abuse potential of stimulants.

doseZones.mechanism: Selective NET inhibitor increasing NE tone. Does not correct why NE is deficient.

Belzutifan.label: Belzutifan
Belzutifan.definition: A HIF-2α inhibitor that reduces transcription of hypoxia-response genes. Proposed experimentally for endothelial HIF-2α dysregulation in post-viral ME/CFS — HIF-2α is upregulated by viral-induced mitochondrial ROS and drives the glycolytic shift and angiogenic imbalance.

doseZones.mechanism: HIF-2α inhibitor. If HIF-2α drives vascular pathology, targets hypoxic signaling cascade. Research-stage.

Canakinumab.label: Canakinumab
Canakinumab.definition: A monoclonal anti-IL-1β antibody that neutralizes IL-1β without affecting IL-1α. Proposed for ME/CFS inflammatory subsets; the CANTOS trial (cardiovascular disease) demonstrated that IL-1β blockade reduces systemic inflammation.

doseZones.mechanism: Blocks IL-1β specifically, interrupting autoinflammatory amplification.

Cilostazol.label: Cilostazol
Cilostazol.definition: A PDE3 inhibitor with vasodilator and antiplatelet effects, used for intermittent claudication. Proposed in ME/CFS for microvascular perfusion deficits — PDE3 inhibition increases cAMP in platelets and vascular smooth muscle, improving blood flow.

doseZones.mechanism: PDE3 inhibitor improving microvascular perfusion. Addresses perfusion deficit without correcting the cause.

Cimetidine.label: Cimetidine
Cimetidine.definition: An H2 receptor antagonist with additional immunomodulatory effects — inhibits suppressor T cells and enhances Th1 responses. Used off-label in ME/CFS for its dual H2 blockade (MCAS) and immunomodulation; also inhibits CYP450 enzymes, increasing levels of many co-prescribed drugs.

doseZones.mechanism: H2 receptor antagonist with T-cell enhancement via H2 on suppressor T cells.

Clopidogrel.label: Clopidogrel
Clopidogrel.definition: A P2Y12 receptor antagonist antiplatelet agent. Proposed in ME/CFS for microclot-mediated hypoperfusion — P2Y12 blockade reduces platelet activation and aggregation triggered by endothelial dysfunction and inflammatory mediators.

doseZones.mechanism: P2Y12 inhibitor reducing platelet aggregation. Research-stage for microthrombi.

Colchicine.label: Colchicine
Colchicine.definition: An anti-inflammatory alkaloid that inhibits microtubule polymerization, blocking NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and neutrophil chemotaxis. Used in gout, pericarditis, and familial Mediterranean fever. Proposed in ME/CFS for NLRP3-driven inflammation; narrow therapeutic window with significant GI toxicity.
Colchicine.class: Anti-inflammatory / microtubule inhibitor / NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitor

doseZones.mechanism: Microtubule inhibitor with NLRP3 inflammasome suppression. Narrow therapeutic window.

Cyclosporine.label: Cyclosporine
Cyclosporine.definition: A calcineurin inhibitor immunosuppressant that blocks NFAT activation and IL-2 production in T cells. Used experimentally as an NFAT pathway probe in ME/CFS — response would implicate T-cell-driven autoimmunity in that patient's endotype.

doseZones.mechanism: Calcineurin inhibitor suppressing T-cell activation. Broad immunosuppression — nephrotoxicity risk.

Daratumumab.label: Daratumumab
Daratumumab.definition: A monoclonal anti-CD38 antibody that depletes plasma cells (including long-lived antibody-secreting plasma cells). A pilot study in ME/CFS reported ~60% response rate, suggesting autoantibody-producing plasma cells may drive pathophysiology in a subset — potentially a disease-modifying treatment for autoimmune ME/CFS.
Daratumumab.class: Monoclonal antibody / anti-CD38 / plasma cell depleting agent

doseZones.mechanism: Depletes CD38+ long-lived plasma cells — targets the source rituximab spares. Research-stage in ME/CFS.

Donepezil.label: Donepezil
Donepezil.definition: A centrally-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used for Alzheimer's disease. Proposed experimentally in ME/CFS to enhance CNS cholinergic tone for cognitive dysfunction — the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway and cognitive enhancement provide dual rationale.

doseZones.mechanism: AChE inhibitor enhancing cholinergic transmission. Cognitive benefit if cholinergic deficiency — GI side effects.

Dornase alfa.label: Dornase alfa
Dornase alfa.definition: Recombinant human DNase I that cleaves extracellular DNA, including neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). Proposed experimentally in ME/CFS for NET degradation in microclot pathology — NET-derived DNA contributes to amyloid fibrin microclot formation.

doseZones.mechanism: DNase enzyme degrading NET DNA. If NETosis confirmed, clears NET-derived DAMPs. Research-stage.

Doxycycline.label: Doxycycline
Doxycycline.definition: A tetracycline antibiotic. At subantimicrobial doses, doxycycline inhibits matrix metalloproteinases (MMP-2, MMP-9), reducing connective tissue degradation. Of interest in ME/CFS/hEDS for MMP-mediated tissue remodeling and blood-brain barrier stabilization.

doseZones.mechanism: MMP inhibition at sub-antimicrobial doses reduces ECM degradation. Does not address what drives MMP-9.

Erythromycin.label: Erythromycin
Erythromycin.definition: A macrolide antibiotic that is also a motilin receptor agonist, stimulating GI motility. Used at low doses in ME/CFS for gastroparesis and GI dysmotility via its prokinetic effects, independent of its antibiotic action.
Erythromycin.class: Macrolide antibiotic / motilin receptor agonist / prokinetic

doseZones.mechanism: Motilin agonist. Prokinetic — tachyphylaxis within 2–4 weeks; QT prolongation risk.

Folinic acid.label: Folinic acid
Folinic acid.definition: 5-Formyltetrahydrofolate (leucovorin): a reduced folate that bypasses the MTHFR step and directly enters the folate cycle. Used in ME/CFS methylation support — particularly in patients with MTHFR polymorphisms who cannot efficiently convert folic acid to active folate. Also supports BH4 recycling.
Folinic acid.brand: Leucovorin, various supplement brands (as calcium folinate)

doseZones.mechanism: Folate derivative. Supports methylation and DNA synthesis.

Glycyrrhizin.label: Glycyrrhizin
Glycyrrhizin.definition: A triterpenoid saponin from licorice root (Glycyrrhiza glabra) that directly binds and inhibits HMGB1, a key DAMP driving TLR4/RAGE-mediated inflammation. Proposed in ME/CFS for HMGB1-driven neuroinflammation. Caution: glycyrrhizin causes pseudohyperaldosteronism (hypertension, hypokalemia) with sustained use.
Glycyrrhizin.rx: OTC (as licorice root extract); prescription (IV glycyrrhizin in Asia)
Glycyrrhizin.brand: Various supplement brands; licorice root extract

doseZones.mechanism: HMGB1 inhibitor targeting a causal DAMP mediator in PEM. Research-stage.

Heparin.label: Heparin
Heparin.definition: A glycosaminoglycan anticoagulant that activates antithrombin III, inhibiting thrombin and factor Xa. Mast cells contain heparin in their granules; endogenous heparin release during MCAS degranulation may contribute to the coagulation abnormalities and bleeding tendencies observed in some ME/CFS patients.

doseZones.mechanism: Anticoagulant reducing microthrombi. If microclots are pathological, targets coagulation cascade. Bleeding risk; research-stage.

Larazotide.label: Larazotide
Larazotide.definition: A zonulin antagonist that prevents tight junction opening in the intestinal epithelium, reducing intestinal permeability ('leaky gut'). Trialled in celiac disease and Long COVID; of interest in ME/CFS for gut barrier dysfunction and metabolic endotoxemia.

doseZones.mechanism: Zonulin antagonist reducing intestinal permeability. If leaky gut drives inflammation, targets structural barrier defect. Research-stage.

Maraviroc.label: Maraviroc
Maraviroc.definition: A CCR5 receptor antagonist preventing monocyte chemotaxis into inflamed tissue. Tested with pravastatin in Long COVID for monocyte-mediated vascular inflammation; of interest in ME/CFS for the monocyte/macrophage-driven neuroinflammatory component.

doseZones.mechanism: CCR5 antagonist. If CCR5-mediated inflammatory cell trafficking drives neuroinflammation, targets specific chemokine pathway. Research-stage.

Methylcobalamin.label: Methylcobalamin
Methylcobalamin.definition: The methylated active form of vitamin B12, directly usable in the methylation cycle (methionine synthase). Used in ME/CFS methylation protocols; preferred over cyanocobalamin in patients with impaired hepatic methylation capacity.
Methylcobalamin.class: Active vitamin B12 / methyl donor cofactor

doseZones.mechanism: Active B12 form. Supports methylation and mitochondrial function without hepatic conversion.

Methylfolate.label: Methylfolate
Methylfolate.definition: L-5-Methyltetrahydrofolate (5-MTHF): the active form of folate that bypasses MTHFR-mediated activation. Used in ME/CFS methylation support protocols; particularly relevant for patients with MTHFR C677T polymorphisms who have reduced capacity to convert folic acid to active methylfolate.

doseZones.mechanism: Active folate form. Bypasses MTHFR-dependent conversion. Supports methylation.

Minocycline.label: Minocycline
Minocycline.definition: A tetracycline antibiotic with unique anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties: inhibits microglial activation, MMPs, and PARP, while reducing IL-1β and TNF-α. Of interest in ME/CFS for neuroinflammation and microglial-mediated sickness behavior; more CNS-penetrant than doxycycline.

doseZones.mechanism: Microglial anti-inflammatory + MMP-9 inhibition + neuroprotective. Multi-mechanism tetracycline.

Nifedipine.label: Nifedipine
Nifedipine.definition: An L-type calcium channel blocker (dihydropyridine) primarily used for hypertension and vasospastic angina. Investigated in ME/CFS for TRPV1-mediated arteriolar vasoconstriction — TRPV1 activation on vascular smooth muscle triggers L-type Ca²⁺ channel opening and vasoconstriction; nifedipine blocks this downstream effect.

doseZones.mechanism: L-type Ca²⁺ channel blocker reducing vasoconstriction. Short half-life limits sustained benefit.

Omalizumab.label: Omalizumab
Omalizumab.definition: A monoclonal anti-IgE antibody that binds free IgE, preventing its binding to FcεRI on mast cells and basophils. Proposed for IgE-mediated MCAS in ME/CFS — only effective in the minority of MCAS patients with documented IgE-mediated allergy.

doseZones.mechanism: Anti-IgE monoclonal antibody blocking IgE-mediated mast cell activation. Targets a specific activation pathway.

Pentoxifylline.label: Pentoxifylline
Pentoxifylline.definition: A xanthine derivative that improves erythrocyte deformability, reduces blood viscosity, and inhibits TNF-α production. Proposed in ME/CFS for microvascular perfusion deficits — improved red blood cell flexibility may enhance oxygen delivery in patients with RBC deformability abnormalities.
Pentoxifylline.class: Hemorrhologic agent / PDE inhibitor / TNF-α inhibitor

doseZones.mechanism: PDE inhibitor reducing blood viscosity and TNF-α. Modulates perfusion/cytokine balance.

Pravastatin.label: Pravastatin
Pravastatin.definition: A hydrophilic HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin) with pleiotropic anti-inflammatory effects independent of cholesterol lowering: reduces monocyte activation, endothelial dysfunction, and CRP. Tested with maraviroc in a Long COVID trial targeting monocyte-mediated vascular inflammation.

doseZones.mechanism: Statin with pleiotropic anti-inflammatory effects. May reduce endothelial inflammation. Muscle symptoms concern in ME/CFS.

Pregnenolone.label: Pregnenolone
Pregnenolone.definition: The precursor neurosteroid from which all other steroid hormones are synthesized. Pregnenolone itself is a TRPM3 agonist and positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A and NMDA receptors. Used in ME/CFS for HPA axis support and neurosteroid-mediated cognitive and mood effects.

Rapamycin.label: Rapamycin
Rapamycin.definition: An mTORC1 inhibitor that enhances autophagy and mitophagy by releasing the mTOR-mediated brake on cellular quality control. Investigated in ME/CFS for clearing damaged mitochondria — impaired mitophagy may be a key driver of mitochondrial dysfunction; rapamycin forces mitochondrial turnover.

doseZones.mechanism: mTORC1-selective autophagy restoration — preserves mTORC2-mediated metabolic functions. Intermittent dosing is key to selectivity.
mTORC2 inhibition adds metabolic side effects, blunting net benefit. Receptor-occupancy threshold crossed.

Rintatolimod.label: Rintatolimod
Rintatolimod.definition: A synthetic double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) that activates TLR3, inducing type I interferon and innate antiviral responses. The only drug to show efficacy in a subset of ME/CFS patients in randomized trials (Ampligen). Hypothesis: chronic low-level viral persistence or defective antiviral response that TLR3 activation corrects.
Rintatolimod.rx: Investigational / limited access (US); not approved in EU

doseZones.mechanism: TLR3 agonist restoring RNase L pathway and innate antiviral immunity. Research-stage.

Roflumilast.label: Roflumilast
Roflumilast.definition: A selective PDE4 inhibitor that increases intracellular cAMP in immune and inflammatory cells, suppressing TNF-α, IL-17, and other pro-inflammatory cytokines. PDE4 inhibition also enhances autophagy. Of interest in ME/CFS for chronic neuroinflammation and impaired autophagic clearance.

doseZones.mechanism: PDE4 inhibitor reducing cAMP degradation. Broad anti-inflammatory — GI side effects limit use.

Sirolimus.label: Sirolimus
Sirolimus.definition: Same as rapamycin — see Rapamycin entry.

doseZones.mechanism: Same as Rapamycin — mTORC1 inhibition restoring autophagy and reducing senescence.

TUDCA.label: TUDCA
TUDCA.definition: Tauroursodeoxycholic Acid: a conjugated bile acid that acts as a chemical chaperone, reducing endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress by stabilizing protein folding and inhibiting the UPR. TUDCA also protects mitochondria from ER stress-induced damage. Of interest in ME/CFS for the documented ER stress/UPR activation in patient cells.
TUDCA.class: Bile acid / chemical chaperone / ER stress reducer

doseZones.mechanism: ER stress reducer stabilizing protein folding and calming UPR. Research-stage in ME/CFS.

Tacrolimus.label: Tacrolimus
Tacrolimus.definition: A calcineurin inhibitor immunosuppressant (structurally distinct from cyclosporine) that blocks NFAT activation. More potent than cyclosporine; used experimentally as an NFAT pathway probe in ME/CFS — response would support T-cell-mediated autoimmunity.

doseZones.mechanism: Calcineurin inhibitor suppressing T-cell activation. Nephrotoxicity risk.

Warfarin.label: Warfarin
Warfarin.definition: A vitamin K antagonist anticoagulant inhibiting synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X. Referenced in ME/CFS microclot context. Narrow therapeutic index requiring regular INR monitoring; significant drug and dietary interactions.

doseZones.mechanism: Vitamin K antagonist reducing coagulation. Narrow therapeutic window; bleeding risk; requires monitoring.

Beta-hydroxybutyrate.label: Beta-hydroxybutyrate
Beta-hydroxybutyrate.definition: β-Hydroxybutyrate (BHB): the primary ketone body, serving as an alternative brain fuel during carbohydrate restriction or fasting. BHB also functions as a signaling molecule — it inhibits HDACs (epigenetic regulation) and activates HCA2/GPR109A (anti-inflammatory). Ketone metabolism may bypass the PDH gate that is impaired in ME/CFS.

Lumbrokinase.label: Lumbrokinase
Lumbrokinase.definition: A fibrinolytic enzyme complex extracted from earthworms (Lumbricus rubellus) that directly degrades fibrin and fibrinogen. Proposed experimentally in ME/CFS for amyloid fibrin microclot degradation to improve microvascular perfusion.

doseZones.mechanism: Fibrinolytic enzyme degrading fibrin microthrombi. Research-stage; limited quality control.

Nattokinase.label: Nattokinase
Nattokinase.definition: A fibrinolytic enzyme from natto (fermented soybeans, Bacillus subtilis) that directly degrades fibrin and also enhances endogenous plasmin production. Proposed in ME/CFS for microclot degradation; structurally similar to lumbrokinase with overlapping mechanism.

doseZones.mechanism: Fibrinolytic enzyme degrading fibrin microthrombi. Research-stage; limited quality control.

MitoQ.label: MitoQ
MitoQ.definition: Mitochondria-targeted ubiquinone: a CoQ10 molecule conjugated to a triphenylphosphonium cation that accumulates in the mitochondrial matrix driven by membrane potential, delivering antioxidant protection at the primary site of ROS production. Proposed in ME/CFS to directly reduce mitochondrial oxidative stress.

doseZones.mechanism: Mitochondria-targeted CoQ10 analog. More efficient mitochondrial delivery than standard CoQ10.

NADH.label: NADH
NADH.definition: Reduced Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide: the electron-carrying form of NAD+ produced by glycolysis and the TCA cycle, feeding electrons into Complex I of the electron transport chain. NADH is available as an oral supplement; used in ME/CFS to support mitochondrial ATP production, though oral bioavailability is debated.

doseZones.mechanism: Supplies NADH as Complex I substrate. Bypasses reduced endogenous production. Does not correct the production defect.

NMN.label: NMN
NMN.definition: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide: a direct NAD+ precursor that enters cells (via Slc12a8 transporter in the gut) and is converted to NAD+ by NMNAT enzymes. NMN supplementation is proposed in ME/CFS to restore NAD+ levels depleted by PARP activation, CD38, and oxidative stress.
NMN.rx: OTC (as supplement; regulatory status varies by country)

doseZones.mechanism: NAD⁺ precursor. Compensates for NAD⁺ depletion. Does not correct the consumption source.

NR.label: NR
NR.definition: Nicotinamide Riboside: a NAD+ precursor that enters cells and is converted to NAD+ via NRK enzymes. Along with NMN, NR is one of the two main NAD+ precursor supplements proposed for ME/CFS energy metabolism support.

doseZones.mechanism: NAD⁺ precursor. Compensates for NAD⁺ depletion.

Palmitoylethanolamide.label: Palmitoylethanolamide
Palmitoylethanolamide.definition: An endogenous fatty acid amide that activates PPAR-α and also desensitizes TRPV1 via an indirect mechanism, producing analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and mast-cell-stabilizing effects. Used in ME/CFS and fibromyalgia for neuropathic pain and neuroinflammation.
Palmitoylethanolamide.class: Endogenous fatty acid amide / PPAR-α agonist / TRPV1 modulator

doseZones.mechanism: Endogenous PPAR-α agonist + mast cell stabilizer. Modulates neuroinflammation through endogenous lipid signaling.

Spermidine.label: Spermidine
Spermidine.definition: A natural polyamine that induces autophagy (cellular self-cleaning) via inhibition of the acetyltransferase EP300. Found in wheat germ, soy, and aged cheese. Proposed in ME/CFS to enhance autophagic clearance of damaged mitochondria and protein aggregates.

doseZones.mechanism: Autophagy inducer supporting cellular renewal. Research-stage; no ME/CFS data.

Sulforaphane.label: Sulforaphane
Sulforaphane.definition: An isothiocyanate from cruciferous vegetables (broccoli sprouts) that is the most potent known dietary activator of NRF2 (the master antioxidant transcription factor). Sulforaphane also inhibits NF-κB and HDACs. Proposed in ME/CFS to restore NRF2-mediated antioxidant defenses that are impaired in the disease.
Sulforaphane.generic: Sulforaphane (as glucoraphanin precursor or sulforaphane extract)

doseZones.mechanism: Nrf2 activator via Keap1 modification. Activates endogenous anti-inflammatory programs.

Urolithin A.label: Urolithin A
Urolithin A.definition: A gut microbiome-derived metabolite of ellagitannins (from pomegranate, walnuts) that induces mitophagy (selective mitochondrial autophagy) via the PINK1/Parkin pathway. Urolithin A improves mitochondrial function in aged muscle; proposed in ME/CFS to clear damaged mitochondria accumulated from impaired mitophagy.

doseZones.mechanism: Mitophagy activator clearing damaged mitochondria. Restores mitochondrial quality control. Research-stage.

Adrenal.label: Adrenal
Adrenal.definition: The adrenal glands sit atop the kidneys and produce cortisol (zona fasciculata), aldosterone (zona glomerulosa), DHEA (zona reticularis), and catecholamines (adrenal medulla). Adrenal dysfunction in ME/CFS includes blunted cortisol output, low DHEA-S, and altered catecholamine secretion — reflecting HPA axis dysregulation.

Calcitonin.label: Calcitonin
Calcitonin.definition: A peptide hormone from thyroid C-cells that lowers blood calcium by inhibiting osteoclast activity. Calcitonin belongs to the calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) family, which includes potent vasodilators implicated in migraine — relevant to ME/CFS headache and vascular symptoms.

Cortisone.label: Cortisone
Cortisone.definition: The inactive 11-keto form of cortisol, converted to active cortisol by 11β-HSD1 in tissues. Cortisone acetate is used therapeutically as a glucocorticoid. The cortisol/cortisone ratio reflects 11β-HSD activity, which may be altered in ME/CFS HPA axis dysfunction.

Insulin.label: Insulin
Insulin.definition: A pancreatic β-cell hormone promoting glucose uptake, glycogenesis, and lipogenesis while inhibiting gluconeogenesis. Insulin resistance has been reported in subsets of ME/CFS, potentially contributing to metabolic inflexibility. Insulin also has CNS effects on cognition and appetite.

Parathyroid.label: Parathyroid
Parathyroid.definition: Four small glands on the thyroid that secrete parathyroid hormone (PTH), regulating calcium and phosphate homeostasis. Hyperparathyroidism can cause fatigue mimicking ME/CFS and must be excluded; hypoparathyroidism can cause neuromuscular irritability resembling ME/CFS muscle symptoms.

Thyroid.label: Thyroid
Thyroid.definition: An endocrine gland in the neck producing thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3), regulating basal metabolic rate. Hypothyroidism produces fatigue that mimics ME/CFS and must be excluded; however, many ME/CFS patients with normal TSH exhibit 'Low T3 Syndrome' — a non-thyroidal illness pattern where peripheral T4→T3 conversion is impaired.

bradykinin.label: bradykinin
bradykinin.definition: A potent vasodilatory and pro-inflammatory peptide of the kallikrein-kinin system that increases vascular permeability and stimulates pain nerve endings. Bradykinin-mediated angioedema overlaps with MCAS histamine-mediated swelling, and bradykinin may contribute to vascular leak and pain in ME/CFS.

substance P.label: substance P
substance P.definition: A neuropeptide neurotransmitter in pain (C-fiber) afferents that transmits nociceptive signals in the dorsal horn. Substance P also directly triggers mast cell degranulation via MRGPRX2, linking neurogenic inflammation to MCAS in ME/CFS — sensory nerve activation releases substance P, which degranulates mast cells, which release more inflammatory mediators, which further sensitize nerves.

Norepinephrine.label: Norepinephrine
Norepinephrine.definition: The primary sympathetic nervous system neurotransmitter and adrenal hormone. Norepinephrine (noradrenaline) drives arousal, vasoconstriction, and cardiac stimulation. Sustained elevated norepinephrine — especially at night — is a hallmark of autonomic dysfunction in ME/CFS, producing the 'tired but wired' state.

Epinephrine.label: Epinephrine
Epinephrine.definition: Adrenaline: the catecholamine hormone released from the adrenal medulla during stress, producing the classic fight-or-flight response. Epinephrine increases heart rate, dilates airways, and mobilizes glucose. Epinephrine surges from MCAS degranulation or POTS sympathetic overactivity may explain the panic-like episodes ME/CFS patients describe.

Babesia.label: Babesia
Babesia.definition: A tick-borne protozoan parasite (Babesia microti, B. divergens) infecting red blood cells, causing babesiosis (fever, hemolytic anemia, fatigue). A known co-infection with Lyme disease; chronic babesiosis can produce ME/CFS-like fatigue and must be considered in the differential diagnosis.

Bartonella.label: Bartonella
Bartonella.definition: A genus of intracellular bacteria causing cat-scratch disease (B. henselae) and trench fever (B. quintana). Tick-borne Bartonella co-infections are common in Lyme disease; chronic Bartonella may cause neuropsychiatric symptoms, fatigue, and vasculitis that overlap with ME/CFS.

Campylobacter.label: Campylobacter
Campylobacter.definition: A bacterial genus (primarily C. jejuni) causing gastroenteritis and a major trigger of Guillain-Barré syndrome via molecular mimicry between bacterial ganglioside-like structures and peripheral nerve antigens. Campylobacter is a model organism for infection-triggered autoimmunity — directly relevant to the post-infectious ME/CFS paradigm.

Clostridium.label: Clostridium
Clostridium.definition: A genus of anaerobic bacteria including C. difficile (antibiotic-associated colitis), a major gut dysbiosis pathogen. Clostridium species produce short-chain fatty acids and secondary bile acids that regulate gut barrier function and immune tolerance — Clostridium depletion in ME/CFS gut dysbiosis may impair these protective functions.

Escherichia coli.label: Escherichia coli
Escherichia coli.definition: A gram-negative enteric bacterium and the most common cause of urinary tract infections (via uropathogenic strains). E. coli LPS is a potent TLR4 agonist; LPS translocation from the gut ('metabolic endotoxemia') is proposed as a driver of low-grade immune activation in ME/CFS with leaky gut.

Klebsiella.label: Klebsiella
Klebsiella.definition: A genus of gram-negative enteric bacteria implicated in gut dysbiosis and molecular mimicry. Klebsiella pneumoniae carries carbohydrate antigens that cross-react with HLA-B27, driving ankylosing spondylitis — a classic example of infection-triggered autoimmunity relevant to ME/CFS autoimmune hypotheses.

Lyme.label: Lyme
Lyme.definition: Lyme disease (Lyme borreliosis): a tick-borne infection caused by Borrelia burgdorferi spirochetes, producing erythema migrans rash, arthritis, neurological symptoms, and carditis. Chronic Lyme disease (PTLDS, post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome) shares substantial clinical overlap with ME/CFS including fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and PEM. The two conditions may coexist — diagnosing ME/CFS in a Lyme patient requires excluding active Borrelia infection.

RSV.label: RSV
RSV.definition: Respiratory Syncytial Virus: a common respiratory virus causing bronchiolitis in infants and cold-like illness in adults. RSV is a documented trigger of post-infectious fatigue and ME/CFS, via the same pathways as other respiratory viruses (immune activation, neuroinvasion, mitochondrial damage).

dengue.label: dengue
dengue.definition: A mosquito-borne flavivirus causing dengue fever (breakbone fever) characterized by severe myalgia, arthralgia, and fatigue. Post-dengue fatigue syndrome is well-documented and clinically overlaps with ME/CFS, providing another post-viral model for ME/CFS pathophysiology.

enterovirus.label: enterovirus
enterovirus.definition: A genus of single-stranded RNA viruses including coxsackievirus and echovirus. Enteroviruses are a leading candidate for persistent viral infection in ME/CFS — enteroviral RNA and VP1 protein have been detected in ME/CFS muscle and gut biopsies, suggesting chronic low-level infection or defective viral clearance.

influenza.label: influenza
influenza.definition: An orthomyxovirus causing seasonal epidemics of respiratory illness. Influenza is a well-documented trigger of post-infectious ME/CFS; the 1918 influenza pandemic produced a wave of 'encephalitis lethargica' with striking ME/CFS-like features including profound fatigue and post-exertional collapse.

pylori.label: H. pylori
pylori.definition: Helicobacter pylori: a gastric bacterium infecting ~50% of the global population, causing chronic gastritis, peptic ulcers, and gastric cancer. H. pylori has been linked to autoimmune conditions (ITP, autoimmune gastritis) via molecular mimicry and chronic immune activation — relevant to ME/CFS autoimmune hypotheses and GI comorbidity.

Chronic Lyme disease.label: Chronic Lyme disease
Chronic Lyme disease.definition: A controversial term for persistent symptoms after Lyme disease treatment. The IDSA defines post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (PTLDS) as persistent fatigue, pain, and cognitive dysfunction after appropriate antibiotic treatment in confirmed Lyme. Chronic Lyme and ME/CFS share substantial symptom overlap; distinguishing them requires thorough infectious disease evaluation.

Encephalitis.label: Encephalitis
Encephalitis.definition: Inflammation of the brain parenchyma, typically caused by viral infection (HSV, enterovirus, arbovirus) or autoimmunity (anti-NMDAR encephalitis, limbic encephalitis). Post-encephalitic fatigue is a well-documented sequela that overlaps with ME/CFS; autoimmune encephalitis can mimic ME/CFS and must be excluded in atypical presentations.

GLUT1 deficiency syndrome.label: GLUT1 deficiency syndrome
GLUT1 deficiency syndrome.definition: A monogenic disorder caused by SLC2A1 mutations impairing glucose transport across the blood-brain barrier (via GLUT1), causing seizures, developmental delay, and movement disorders. GLUT1 deficiency serves as a model for brain energy failure: if glucose can't enter the brain, symptoms mimic severe ME/CFS including exercise-induced worsening. Relevant to ME/CFS cerebral hypometabolism.

Herpes simplex encephalitis.label: Herpes simplex encephalitis
Herpes simplex encephalitis.definition: HSV-1 infection of the brain causing necrotizing encephalitis, primarily in the temporal lobes. A landmark model for infection-triggered autoimmunity: ~25% of patients develop anti-NMDAR antibodies (via molecular mimicry between HSV and NMDA receptor), causing autoimmune encephalitis months after the infection clears — directly relevant to post-infectious ME/CFS autoimmune mechanisms.

Hidradenitis suppurativa.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
Hidradenitis suppurativa.definition: A chronic inflammatory skin disease of hair follicles in intertriginous areas (axillae, groin), causing painful nodules, abscesses, and sinus tracts. Proposed as an ME/CFS comorbidity via shared inflammatory pathways (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-17) and potential mast cell involvement.

Idiopathic chronic fatigue.label: Idiopathic chronic fatigue
Idiopathic chronic fatigue.definition: Persistent fatigue not meeting ME/CFS diagnostic criteria and not attributable to another condition. ICF lacks PEM — the cardinal ME/CFS symptom. The 2-day CPET distinguishes ICF from ME/CFS: only ME/CFS patients show a significant drop in VO₂ peak and workload at anaerobic threshold on day 2.

Low T3 syndrome.label: Low T3 syndrome
Low T3 syndrome.definition: Non-thyroidal illness syndrome (sick euthyroid syndrome): a pattern of low serum T3 with normal TSH and T4, reflecting impaired peripheral T4→T3 conversion during systemic illness. Well-documented in ME/CFS; may represent an adaptive energy-conservation response rather than true hypothyroidism. TSH is normal — this is NOT primary thyroid disease.

Overtraining syndrome.label: Overtraining syndrome
Overtraining syndrome.definition: A condition in athletes caused by excessive training with inadequate recovery, characterized by performance decline, persistent fatigue, mood disturbance, and autonomic dysfunction. OTS shares features with early ME/CFS (pre-hysteresis stage) — the transition from functional overreaching → OTS → ME/CFS may represent a single disease trajectory once the hysteresis threshold is crossed.

Periodontitis.label: Periodontitis
Periodontitis.definition: Chronic inflammatory destruction of tooth-supporting tissues driven by bacterial biofilm and host immune responses. Proposed as a model for IgE-mediated connective tissue degradation relevant to the MCAS-hEDS hypothesis in ME/CFS: mast cell degranulation in gingival tissue releases tryptase and MMPs that degrade collagen.

Sickle cell disease.label: Sickle cell disease
Sickle cell disease.definition: A hemoglobinopathy where mutated hemoglobin S polymerizes under low oxygen, causing erythrocyte sickling, vaso-occlusive crises, and chronic hemolytic anemia. TRPV1-mediated vasoconstriction and lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) signaling contribute to vaso-occlusion — a parallel to the TRPV1-driven microvascular constriction model in ME/CFS PEM.

Sjogren syndrome.label: Sjögren syndrome
Sjogren syndrome.definition: An autoimmune disease targeting exocrine glands (salivary, lacrimal), causing dry mouth (xerostomia) and dry eyes (xerophthalmia), with severe fatigue, joint pain, and systemic manifestations. Sjögren's is an important differential diagnosis for ME/CFS — fatigue is the most disabling symptom, and both conditions can coexist. Anti-SSA/Ro and anti-SSB/La antibodies are diagnostic.

Long COVID.label: Long COVID
Long COVID.definition: Post-COVID-19 condition (PASC): persistent symptoms ≥3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, including fatigue, PEM, brain fog, orthostatic intolerance, and sleep disturbance. ~43-58% of Long COVID patients meet ME/CFS diagnostic criteria; Long COVID has created the largest-ever cohort of post-viral ME/CFS and provides an unprecedented opportunity to study ME/CFS pathophysiology from a known infectious trigger.

Baroreceptor.label: Baroreceptor
Baroreceptor.definition: Stretch-sensitive nerve endings in the carotid sinus and aortic arch that detect blood pressure changes, forming the afferent limb of the baroreflex. Baroreflex dysfunction in ME/CFS impairs the ability to maintain blood pressure when upright, directly contributing to orthostatic intolerance.

Carotid body.label: Carotid body
Carotid body.definition: A small cluster of chemoreceptor cells at the carotid artery bifurcation that senses blood oxygen, CO₂, and pH, driving ventilatory responses to hypoxia. Carotid body dysfunction has been proposed in ME/CFS dysautonomia — inappropriate chemoreflex activation could drive hyperventilation and sympathetic overactivation.

Chemoreceptor.label: Chemoreceptor
Chemoreceptor.definition: Sensory receptors detecting chemical changes in blood or interstitial fluid. Peripheral chemoreceptors in the carotid and aortic bodies sense O₂/CO₂/pH; central chemoreceptors in the brainstem sense CO₂/pH. Chemoreflex hypersensitivity may contribute to hyperventilation and dyspnea in ME/CFS.

Endotheliopathy.label: Endotheliopathy
Endotheliopathy.definition: A disease state of endothelial cell dysfunction encompassing impaired NO-mediated vasodilation, increased adhesion molecule expression, loss of glycocalyx, and a shift toward a pro-coagulant/pro-inflammatory phenotype. Endotheliopathy is proposed as a central mechanism in ME/CFS explaining microvascular hypoperfusion, exercise intolerance, and multisystem involvement.

Glymphatic system.label: Glymphatic system
Glymphatic system.definition: The brain's perivascular waste clearance system: CSF flows along periarterial spaces into the brain interstitium, driven by arterial pulsatility and AQP4 channels on astrocyte end-feet, then exits via perivenous routes carrying metabolic waste (amyloid-β, tau, lactate).
